clue.text: A Belgian winner of the Nobel prize

definitions.meaning: a native of Flanders, the Dutch-speaking north of Belgium
Sir Alexander ... shared the 1945 Nobel prize in medicine for penicillin

explanation.surface: A Belgian laureate is being introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a Flemish person from Flanders; the other is the Scottish scientist who discovered penicillin and won a Nobel prize.

clue.text: Workers following a standard being set in Arizona

indicators.note: following means the workers come after the standard

parts.note: a standard is a flag
a staff is a body of workers

explanation.surface: Employees follow a flag being raised in Arizona.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'following' makes STAFF come after FLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstaff is a city in northern Arizona.

clue.text: … feel USA might well be agreeable

indicators.note: might well be suggests these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Americans may find the sensation pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from 1-down; 'might well be' rearranges FEELUSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Easeful means comfortable and soothing, pleasant to experience.

clue.text: Brown is in consequence grave

indicators.note: is in means the colour goes inside the word for consequence

parts.note: import means consequence or significance
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: Brown is a serious figure as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' is the adjective serious, not a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave matters are weighty, serious ones.

clue.text: Take a breath and settle up quietly

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to sag is to settle or sink
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Inhale and pay the bill softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle up' looks like paying a bill; SAG reads upwards as GAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw in breath sharply.

clue.text: Space — it is unusually germ-free

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the words before it are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Outer space is, oddly, free of germs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges SPACE plus IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile, with no harmful bacteria present, as in a surgical setting.

clue.text: A member of the opposition not against reform

indicators.note: reform means the letters of the words before it are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: An opposition MP who is not against reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges NOTAGAINST.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent or adversary, one who fights against you.

clue.text: A flier for instance concerned with taxying initially

parts.note: e.g. stands for exempli gratia, for instance
re means about, concerned with

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word taxying

explanation.surface: A plane, say, taxiing along the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests an aircraft; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is anything that flies; this one is a white heron.

clue.text: Article about first sovereign certainly has its points

indicators.note: about means the article goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the is the definite article
first written as 1st, with I standing for 1
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L stands for the pound

explanation.surface: A piece on an early monarch definitely has merits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has its points' looks like having merits; here it means prickles.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly plant, covered in sharp spines.

clue.text: The persuasion of many a grass

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: Many people believe in grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'persuasion' is a noun for a belief system, not the act of persuading.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuasion is a religious faith or set of beliefs.

clue.text: A recurrent attitude for the moralist

indicators.note: recurrent read as running back, so the word for attitude is read from its end

parts.note: a pose is an attitude struck

explanation.surface: A habitual stance suits someone who preaches morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrent' turns POSE into ESOP after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist whose animal stories each end with a moral.

clue.text: Morose but sensible about change one's made

indicators.note: about means the word for sensible goes around the other pieces

parts.note: sane means sensible
turn means change, as in the tide turning
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A gloomy but level-headed person thinks about the change they have made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TURN and I inside SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sullen temperament, once blamed on the planet Saturn.

clue.text: It'S a moving experience, viewing animals in the wild

definitions.text: It'S a moving experience, viewing animals in the wild

parts.words: It'S a moving experience, viewing animals in the wild
parts.note: an emotionally moving experience in the surface, but literally a journey on the move to watch wild animals

explanation.surface: Watching wildlife is a touching experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' means travelling, not stirring the emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedition, typically in Africa, to observe or hunt wild animals in their habitat.

clue.text: Relaxed converse

parts.note: converse looks like a verb meaning chat, but here it is a noun: the opposite of relaxed

explanation.surface: People chatting at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converse' reads as a verb (talk), but it is the noun meaning opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated, flustered and tense, is the opposite state to being calm and at ease.

clue.text: Notes the answer could be indulgence

parts.note: A and B are musical notes
a solution is an answer

explanation.surface: Notes suggest that pardon could be the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Catholic Church, an indulgence remits punishment for sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is forgiveness of sins, akin to a granted pardon or indulgence.

clue.text: Some habitual loafers may be seen in this Scottish place

definitions.text: may be seen in this Scottish place

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Idlers are a common sight in a certain Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in central Scotland, on the River Forth.

clue.text: Players love to look sly in military gear

parts.note: a band is a group of musical players
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to leer is to look slyly or lecherously

explanation.surface: Musicians enjoy smirking at soldiers' kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as O comes from tennis scoring, where love is nil.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder belt with loops or pockets for carrying cartridges, worn by soldiers.

clue.text: Gifts of iron hoops

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
rings are hoops

explanation.surface: Presents made of metal hoops.
explanation.definitionFit: Offerings are things given, presents or contributions.

clue.text: Fundamental reason to limit drink supplies

parts.note: to ration is to limit supply
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: The basic reason for restricting supplies of alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying logic or justification behind something.

clue.text: Cross at finding debts to be paid following French do

indicators.note: following means the debts come after the other pieces

parts.note: to act is to do
an IOU is a note acknowledging a debt, so IOUs are debts

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed to discover unpaid bills after a French party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party (a French do), but it is the verb, giving ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and quarrelsome, the way a cross person is.

clue.text: State overtime is quite usual

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
read as over time: age is a long time, and in a down clue AVER sits over it

explanation.surface: Working extra hours is normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overtime' must be split into 'over time': AVER on top of AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means ordinary, typical, middling.

clue.text: Spread quickly around the Orient

indicators.note: around means the word for quickly surrounds the other piece

parts.note: fast means quickly
E is East, the Orient

explanation.surface: A rapid expansion round the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' is a noun here, a lavish meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a large meal laid out, a banquet.

clue.text: A lover — married, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters of the word before are disordered

explanation.surface: A sweetheart who sadly turns out to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges MARRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a suitor, someone romantically attracted.

clue.text: Get rid of listening device hidden in cuff

indicators.note: hidden in means one piece is tucked inside the other

parts.note: a clout is a cuff, a blow
the ear is the body's own listening device

explanation.surface: Dispose of a bug concealed in a shirt cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening device' suggests a bug and 'cuff' a sleeve; they are EAR and a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear out is to empty a place by throwing unwanted things away.

clue.text: The queen maybe going round little hospital in Somerset

indicators.note: going round means the playing card surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a queen is one example of a playing card
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Royalty visits a small hospital in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The queen' is a playing card. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a market town in Somerset, England.

clue.text: Bill, being in debt, is hustled

indicators.note: being in means the bill sits inside the word for debt

parts.note: in the red means in debt
ac is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A man named Bill, being in debt, is pushed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is AC, an account.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hustled along is to be hurried, rushed.

clue.text: Beat down blockhead in business — it's all a game

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the word for business

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
to ram is to beat down, as earth is rammed
the head of block is its first letter, B

explanation.surface: Thumping an idiot at work is all just a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhead' is not a fool: it is the head of 'block'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crambo is an old word game in which players find rhymes for a given word.

clue.text: Move when it's cooler

definitions.meaning: the cooler is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Get going when the weather turns colder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' is slang for prison, not lower temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring means shifting or budging, and stir is old slang for jail, like the cooler.

clue.text: A ragged shirt can indicate a malcontent

indicators.note: ragged means the letters of the following words are torn about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wearing a tattered shirt marks someone out as a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' rearranges SHIRTCAN to NARCHIST after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel opposed to all government, an extreme kind of discontented agitator.

clue.text: 19 standing by a woman

parts.note: 19-down is AVERAGE, and the norm is the average

explanation.surface: Someone stands by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The number refers to the answer at 19-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, best known from Bellini's opera heroine.

clue.text: China Town

definitions.meaning: porcelain made at Meissen near the German city is sold under the city's name
a city in eastern Germany, capital of Saxony

explanation.surface: A Chinatown.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain from Saxony takes the name of the German city where it was sold.

clue.text: To give another helping would be extra

definitions.meaning: to dish up food a second time
a spare or substitute kept back

explanation.surface: Second helpings would be excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SERVE for the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving again is re-serving, and a reserve is a spare kept in hand.
